open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes
open_points.text: Inputs: “One JSON value.” Errors: “refused for … a duplicate key.” The conventions instead say surface turns “every JSON text” into canonical form.
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text so it can detect duplicate object keys, or an already-parsed JSON value where duplicate keys are no longer observable?
options: Accept raw JSON text and parse it with duplicate-key detection
Accept a parsed value and require duplicate-key detection before this operation
Provide separate operations for parsing text and canonicalizing a parsed value
open_points.default_guess: Accept raw JSON text and perform duplicate-key detection while parsing.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.fit_port_value
open_points.text: “its size bound applying to the whole value”
open_points.question: For a value-carriage candidate, which byte representation is measured against the size bound?
options: RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes
The request's original JSON bytes
A runtime-specific serialized or in-memory size
open_points.default_guess: Measure the RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes.

open_points.subject: store.page_records
open_points.text: “the next continuation token when more remain” together with “The filter is applied as of each page's request: a record whose filtered field changed since an earlier page is judged by its value now”
open_points.question: Does “more remain” mean more records matching the filter now, or any unscanned records below the page position that could match after a mutable status changes?
options: Return a token only when another record currently matches
Return a token while any unscanned record exists, permitting empty pages
Snapshot filter membership when the first page is read
open_points.default_guess: Return a token while any unscanned record exists so later status changes below the position remain observable.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list
open_points.text: “Re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read; … a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes”
open_points.question: After a failed re-read, what forces another re-read if the file becomes readable with bytes whose digest equals the last successfully loaded file, or if the same bytes become parseable only after a transient read failure?
options: Re-read on every request while no valid list exists
Track the failed bytes' digest and re-read only after it changes
Keep comparing against the last successful digest without a special no-list rule
open_points.default_guess: Re-read on every request while no valid token list exists.

open_points.subject: service response output limits
open_points.text: A09 says a 2xx response is contract_violation when “the body exceeds service_response_bytes_max, stored_value_bytes_max or the spool ceilings”; A15 says “A value a node produces … above stored_value_bytes_max” fails, while files use spool_file_bytes_max and spool_run_bytes_max.
open_points.question: Which limits apply to a JSON response with several output members and which apply to a file response: the whole body, each produced StoredValue, or both?
options: Apply stored_value_bytes_max to the entire response body, including file bodies
Apply stored_value_bytes_max separately to each value output and spool ceilings only to file outputs
Apply stored_value_bytes_max to the whole JSON body but exempt file bodies
open_points.default_guess: Apply service_response_bytes_max to every body, stored_value_bytes_max separately to each value output, and spool ceilings to file outputs.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file
open_points.text: “refused over a spool ceiling, nothing kept of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before” and “A link or an I/O failure is internal_error with nothing kept of that file.”
open_points.question: If a ceiling refusal requires deleting files already spooled for the attempt and that deletion fails, what result is returned and which files are allowed to remain?
options: Return internal_error and allow unreferenced attempt files to remain for startup cleanup
Return refused even if cleanup failed
Make the ceiling check reserve the whole attempt before any file is published
open_points.default_guess: Return internal_error; leave any undeletable files unreferenced and remove them during startup cleanup.

open_points.subject: effects.operation_element_conclusion
open_points.text: “Read from the NodeExecution and EffectAttempt together”
open_points.question: When an element has several NodeExecutions and EffectAttempts because it was resumed or resent, which records determine its current conclusion, and how are older unknown attempts resolved not_applied excluded?
options: Use the highest attempt_number and its associated records
Use the newest records in store order regardless of attempt_number
Fold the complete history with an explicitly defined precedence
open_points.default_guess: Use the highest attempt_number, consulting that attempt's EffectAttempt resolution when present.
